entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word for the feeling, with no reservation in it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Procedural warmth only: someone has testified, and that is all it claims.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises dependability rather than brilliance - built to last.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word, and the honest one: approval expressed and meant.
examples: The parents praised their children for their academic performance

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal condemnation by a body; the weight comes from the institution.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Half-hidden laughter at someone's expense - sly and mean.

entries.definition: with sternness; in a severe manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *stern*: the face more than the rule; sternness is something the other person can see.

entries.definition: showing or motivated by sympathy and understanding and generosity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Kindness without self-protection - the giver is not holding anything back.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Nothing held back and nothing divided; rare and slightly archaic.

entries.definition: die, as in battle or in a hunt
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Death in battle, framed as honourable - the word on war memorials.
examples: Several deer have fallen to the same gun

entries.definition: slow to learn or understand; lacking intellectual acuity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Harsh and casual; also an older, now offensive word for mute.
examples: dumb officials make some really dumb decisions

entries.definition: worn or shabby from overuse or (of pages) from having corners turned down
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The one word here that is nearly affectionate - a dog-eared book was loved.
examples: a somewhat dog-eared duke … a bit run down
an old book with dog-eared pages

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *genial*: warmth that puts a room at ease.

entries.definition: tenaciously unwilling or marked by tenacious unwillingness to yield
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Colder and more formal than stubborn; it withholds the affection stubborn allows.

entries.definition: (of persons or their actions) able or disposed to inflict pain or suffering
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries a colonial history of describing whole peoples; strongest when kept for acts.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Old-fashioned and slightly schoolroom - it praises training more than instinct.

entries.definition: based on hypothesis or theory rather than experiment
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal; in everyday use it can hint that a belief was formed before looking at the facts.
examples: Her objections were a priori - she had not read the report.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Clears the bar and no more; in speech it often signals mild disappointment.

entries.definition: with speculation; in a speculative manner
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The adverb of *speculative*: curiosity aimed at ideas rather than people, and neutral for it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and disdainful: economy pursued past the point of dignity.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Affectionate scolding - too light to carry a real fault.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Wholehearted laughter - the room joins in.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *uncouth*: once simply *unknown*; the strangeness curdled into rudeness.
examples: uncouthly, he told stories that made everybody at the table wince

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: An old sense - to sing something in a full round voice; the modern internet sense is unrelated.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same claim with more disapproval attached.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Describes the habit of giving easily, with no comment on why.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mercy was available and was withheld; that is the entire charge.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Slides between stingy and shoddy; either way it is a sneer at what was provided.

entries.definition: sufficiently fat so as to have a pleasing fullness of figure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Mild and often affectionate, especially of children - the least loaded word here.
examples: a chubby baby with dimpled hands

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Emphatic disapproval with a formal, slightly literary edge.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the looker outright: the look is sexual, unwanted and obvious.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Infested rather than soiled, which most readers find the worse of the two.

entries.definition: not having enough money to pay for necessities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Genteel and bookish - poverty at a polite distance.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most vivid of the fists - the hand is shut and stays shut.

entries.definition: designed to deceive or mislead either deliberately or inadvertently
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mild because it does not require a liar - a shadow or a photograph can be deceptive.
examples: the deceptive calm in the eye of the storm

entries.definition: openly distrustful and unwilling to confide
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Built as a plain negative, and it sounds like a diagnosis.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Crude and mocking.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Legal Latin, and it is about standing rather than feeling.

entries.definition: polished and well-groomed; showing sophisticated elegance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The feminine French form, and the commoner spelling in English.

entries.definition: find fault with; express criticism of; point out real or perceived flaws
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The British spelling of the same neutral verb.

entries.definition: emotionlessly and heartlessly; with deliberate cruelty or callousness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *cold-blooded*: premeditation is the whole charge - the harm was planned while calm.
examples: he cold-bloodedly planned the murder of his boss

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely factual: not currently occupied, with no view taken on why.
examples: the cancellation left her unengaged a good part of the afternoon

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Scots for a cosy, unforced warmth; affectionate and close to untranslatable.

entries.definition: express complaints, discontent, displeasure, or unhappiness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The neutral verb - it records the act and leaves the merits open.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Plain and unliterary, and it complains about the thing rather than sneering at it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *rapacious*: appetite as plunder - it has left the table and taken to taking.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Of portions and allowances, not politics - though the political sense now shadows every use.
examples: a liberal backer of the arts

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Political and accusing - it belongs to arguments about who deserves support.
examples: the unemployed are not necessarily work-shy
